content.text: The verifier's guidance is now clear: silence is better than the preferred position, and my inserted clause would have created an audit right and cost-shifting obligation that does not exist today. Reverting to the compliant finding with no redline.

input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale: Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verif" and "books" return no hits, and a full read of the Agreement (single section, p0000–p0074) confirms Kubient has no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against The Associated Press and no right of direct or remote access to our systems. The only access obligation on us (p0001) is a cooperation covenant to enable Kubient to deliver the Services, and the fee mechanics in section 5 (p0023) impose no verification right or audit cost-shifting on us; indeed Kubient contracts with Advertisers and remits to us, so an "underpayment by Customer" audit mechanic is largely inapposite here. This rule is a protective limitation on Vendor audit rights, so genuine silence leaves us better off than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no system access). Inserting an audit framework would be counterproductive, implicitly acknowledging an audit right and cost obligation that do not exist today, so no redline is proposed. If Kubient later proposes an audit clause, we should hold it to the preferred parameters and delete any system-access language.
